newsitem.title: USA: Halliburton says Amoco suit without merit.
newsitem.headline: Halliburton says Amoco suit without merit.

text.p: HOUSTON, Halliburton Co's subsidiary Landmark Graphics Corp said the patent infringement suit Amoco Corp filed against it in federal court July 8 is without merit.
The company said it intends to defend its contractual right to sell its Continuity Cube software to its customers.
Landmark said July 8 the suit seeks damages and a court order to prevent Landmark from distributing the software, which Amoco claims violates its patent.
The company said it has a contractual right to distribute the software under a 1991 agreement between Amoco and Advance Geophysical Corp, which Landmark bought in 1994.

Landmark also said another defendant named in the suit, CAEX Services Inc, is not owned or controlled by Landmark or its parent Halliburton. The company said the Amoco suit wrongly identified CAEX as a wholly-owned subsidiary of Landmark.
Landmark said the suit was filed in the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Oklahoma.
